# Area map: the board (card graph), cards, vocabulary, selection and the tray (webview). Current system as of HEAD 187673d plus the working tree

All paths are relative to `/home/zhengyew/telelean`. Everything here is read from the code; I ran nothing. Where the docs disagree with the code, the code is authoritative (see §7).

## 0. Screen layout (packages/webview/src/App.tsx L12-33)
From top to bottom:
1. **Header**, `.tl-toolbar` (header/Header.tsx L69-85).
2. **LeanBanner**: syntactic mode or checking switched off.
3. **RunElsewhere**: "Claude’s run on **S**: … `Show`".
4. **ProposalBanner**: only while this subject's proposal is in review.
5. `.tl-workspace`: [**Board** + **Toasts**] beside (or, on a narrow board, above) the **RunPanel**.
6. **SelectionTray**.
7. **PromptBox**, the A|D|G box.
8. **Dialogs**: modal, one at a time.

## 1. Every kind of thing that appears on the board

### 1.1 Columns (board/Column.tsx)
- There are three columns, in `NODE_TYPES` order. Titles (labels.ts L8-12): "Assumptions", "Derivations", "Goals". Each header has:
  - the kind glyph **A**/**D**/**G** (labels.ts L21-25);
  - a count badge `.tl-col__count` that counts **cards only**, not vocabulary or ghosts (Column.tsx L82);
  - during a cross-column drag, "Drop to make <Kind>" (L83) and a drop zone that states the D-11 impact, e.g. "Make Derivation: promotion pending until proved" (L29-40, L108);
  - the edge-engine stub badges "▲ n linked" / "▼ n linked", with aria-label "n linked cards above/below; scroll to the nearest" (EdgeEngine.ts L358-361).
- **Order inside the Assumptions column** (Column.tsx L95-100):
  1. `GhostCards` ("Claude suggests", proposed view only);
  2. `VocabularyGroup`;
  3. the cards.

  The Derivations and Goals columns hold cards only. The Vocabulary group exists **only in the Assumptions column**.
- Empty column: "No assumptions yet" / "No derivations yet" / "No goals yet". On a board with no cards at all it adds ": type your first one in the box below" (L102-106).
- Before the first graph arrives: "Waiting for the extension to send the graph…" (Board.tsx L170).

### 1.2 Cards: A / D / G (board/NodeCard.tsx)
All three kinds use one component. The kind is shown by the column, the glyph (`.tl-glyph[data-kind]`) and a 4px left stripe in the kind colour (`.tl-card::before`, board.css L332-341).

**Card face** (L207-291):
- An optional diff line (proposed view only).
- The sentence `naturalName`. If `provenance.wordedBy === 'agent'` it is italic with the marker " (Claude's wording)" (L226-229).
- A check glyph while selected (`codicon-check`, title "Selected", L231), the kind glyph, and a chevron. Chevron aria-labels: "Show Lean code and details" / "Hide details".
- "because: <rationale>" (L263-265).
- Status chips: `cardChips`, model/cardData.ts L140-178.
- A "needs attention" badge `⚠ N`, which expands the card.
- "saving…" while the card is provisional.
- For formalised cards, the "uses:" line (UsesLine, L292).
- The expanded part (CardDetails, L293).

**Status chips** (exact labels):
- Lean status: "λ Lean" / "Lean problem" / "no Lean yet".
- Proof status: "assumed", "✓ proved" (the ✓ is dropped when the card is not checked), "✓ proved: make Derivation?" (a button), "conditional on …", "promotion pending", "unproved".
- Freshness: "changed since last check" / "checking…", and "not checked by Lean".
- Problems and flags: "uses sorry", ".holds says something else", "missing .holds", "rests on a claimed node", "has a proof: make Derivation?" (a button), "self-evident", "existence commitment", "definitional choice", "broken".
- Reason: "no reason yet" / "no source yet" (a button that opens the reason editor).
- "you think this follows from those: prove it?"
- In the proposed view, before the result is revealed, the proof chips are replaced by "result after the review" (NodeCard L21-27, L122-127).

### 1.3 Ghost cards: "Claude suggests" (board/GhostCards.tsx, run/GhostSuggestion.tsx)
- They appear only in the **proposed view**, at the top of the Assumptions column (and in the report card). They are `GhostView`s, not model nodes:
  - no `data-node-id`, so arrows never attach (GhostCards.tsx L1-5);
  - not selectable: `onClick={stop}`, L44.
- Content:
  - the marker "Claude suggests";
  - Claude's sentence, italic, with the agent marker;
  - "Why it is needed:" followed by Claude's text;
  - the Lean proposition (`<pre>`);
  - chips "closes the gap (checked)", "gives the goal on its own: it may simply restate it" and the Lean name.
- Buttons:
  - "I hold this" opens an optional reason field (placeholder "Why do you hold it? (optional)") with "Adopt" / "Cancel";
  - "No".
  - Both work only while `run.state === 'review'` and no request is busy (L19).
- Adopting starts a new round, and the ghost becomes a real ASSUMPTION card in Claude's working copy, with `worded_by: agent`.

### 1.4 Vocabulary group (board/VocabularyGroup.tsx; data from core/src/project/vocabulary.ts and build.ts)
**What it contains.** One item for every declaration in the subject's modules that is **bound to no card**. Excluded (build.ts L341-392):
- declarations owned by a card: its statement, its `.holds`, and any extra `lean:` pinned names (L355-360, L374);
- `example` and `mutual` (L371);
- folded auxiliaries with a facts `parent`, such as structure fields and constructors (L375-378), which show inside their parent item.

The board also lists items **from other subjects** that this subject's cards use. These are read-only and shown under their full name (subjectGraph.ts L33-47).

**Header** (L189-206): the toggle "Vocabulary" with the item count, "+N new" (proposed view; title "Vocabulary the proposal adds"), and "N hidden assumption(s)" (title "Prop-valued axioms with no card (TL104)").

**Sections, in display order** (labels.ts L61-71; classification in vocabulary.ts `classify` L200-279):

| kind | Section title (exact) | Lean declarations that fall into it |
|---|---|---|
| `sort` | **Types** | `axiom T : Type` (type exactly `Type`) |
| `predicate` | **Predicates & relations** | `axiom`/`opaque` whose type ends in `Prop` (arity = number of arguments; 0 allowed). Flag "shape" (TL111) when an argument is not a sort or binders are implicit |
| `function` | **Functions** | `axiom`/`opaque` of type `A₁ → … → B` where every part is a sort. With `axiom`: TL111 "declare it `noncomputable opaque`" |
| `constant` | **Constants** | `opaque c : T` (T a sort). `axiom c : T` gives the same kind plus TL111 |
| `presupposition` | **Presuppositions** | `axiom X : Nonempty T` with T a sort. Rendered as chips, not boxes. The plumbing `instance : Nonempty T := T.exists` is **hidden** (L264-269) |
| `definition` | **Definitions** | `def`, `abbrev`, `structure`, `inductive`/`coinductive`, `class`/`class inductive`/`class abbrev`, and any `instance` except the presupposition instance (L264-275; keywordKind in factsIndex.ts L23-48). This includes **untracked Prop statements**: a Prop-valued def/abbrev with no block (m1-plan 6.4) |
| `lemma` | **Lemmas** | `theorem`/`lemma` with no block |
| `unmarked-axiom` | **Unmarked axioms** | a Prop-valued axiom that is not a card's `.holds`. Flag "hidden assumption" (warning, TL104); also counted in the header chip |
| `other` | **Other** | any other axiom or opaque (with TL111), and other declaration kinds |

**Item box** (`VocabBox`, L77-144):
- shortName (mono, bold), type (`#check`, full names), and a chevron (aria "Show X's code and who uses it" / "Hide X's code");
- the gloss (the docstring);
- flag chips (FLAG_TEXT L36-42): "hidden assumption", "shape", "definition on a statement path" (title "A definition your statements rely on (D-4: needs your endorsement)", not a warning), "changed since last check", "new";
- expanded: the source code (plain `<pre class="tl-lean">`, **without** clickable identifiers), "Used by" (cards, each a button that reveals the card; or "No card uses it yet."), and "Open in editor".

**Presupposition chips in the group** (L146-169) are `<span>`s and **not clickable**. Label: "assumes <sort gloss> exist" or "assumes there is a <Sort>" (cardData.ts L53-61).

**Proposed view:** shows the proposal's vocabulary with diff marks: "New in the proposal" / "Changed in the proposal" / "Removed by the proposal".

### 1.5 Presupposition chips appear in four places
1. The Vocabulary group (not clickable).
2. The tray: "+ presupposes:" buttons that highlight the item (SelectionTray L171-180).
3. The expanded card's "Rests on": buttons that highlight (CardDetails L199-202).
4. The expanded card's "Presupposes" section: buttons (L215-226).

### 1.6 Arrows (board/edges.ts, Board.tsx EdgeDefs, EdgeEngine.ts)
- One arrow per (source, target) pair.
- **Declared** (`premises:`): dashed.
- **Verified** (the proof uses it): solid.
- **Conditional**: a hollow head, with the tooltip "Taken as a hypothesis: the proof is conditional on it".
- **Mismatch**: warning colour, with a tooltip for TL109 or TL107.
- **Reference** (`lean-ref`, one statement mentions another): thin, drawn **only while one end is hovered or selected** and no other arrow joins the pair.
- **Focus**: arrows touching selected or hovered cards use the focusBorder colour and are thicker.
- Arrows join **cards only**. There are no arrows to vocabulary items, definitions or ghosts.

### 1.7 Overlay in the proposed view (model/run.ts `buildOverlay` L595-631)
- The proposal's graph, plus the removed cards and vocabulary drawn with "−".
- Diff mark on each changed card: glyph + word + colour + halo ("+ new", "~ changed", "− removed").
- Cards whose result is hidden lose their result chips and footprint, and verified arrows into them are not drawn.
- The column lists get a faint tint (board.css L1454).

## 2. Where Lean definitions appear on the board (Q3)

**Component and place.** `VocabularyGroup.tsx` → section "Definitions" (`VOCAB_SECTIONS` kind `definition`). It is an item of the **Assumptions column's** list, after any ghosts and before the cards. Within the group, "Definitions" sits between "Presuppositions" and "Lemmas". There is no Definitions column and no definition card.

**When it shows:**
- The group renders only if the board has at least one vocabulary item (`if (items.length === 0) return null`, L183).
- The section renders only if at least one item is a `definition` (L179-182).
- The group is **collapsed by default**: `vocabCollapsed: options.persisted?.vocabCollapsed ?? true` (store.ts L1005-1006). That state is per panel, kept in the VS Code webview state (decisions-log L132).
- It opens when the user clicks "Vocabulary", or when anything calls `highlightVocab` (store.ts L1594-1602, which also persists "open"). In the proposed view it opens by itself when the proposal adds any vocabulary (`vocabularyCollapsed`, store.ts L490-494).

**Getting from a card to its definitions:**
1. **"uses:" line** (UsesLine.tsx):
   - shows "uses: A, B, …" (the first two of `lean.uses`, the statement closure, which includes definitions and the vocabulary they use transitively; build.ts L483-505);
   - "▾ N" opens a menu ("Vocabulary this card uses") listing each item with its kind word ("definition") and gloss;
   - choosing one runs `highlightVocab`: the group opens, the Assumptions column scrolls to the item, and it flashes for 2 s.
   - Items outside this subject's vocabulary are disabled ("X is not in this subject's vocabulary", kind "elsewhere").
2. **Identifiers in the expanded Lean code** (LeanCode.tsx):
   - hovering a dotted-underlined identifier shows a tooltip: the gloss (or short name) and "definition · <name> : <type>";
   - clicking highlights the item in the group;
   - Ctrl/Cmd+click does nothing (reserved).
   - These links exist only when the file's Lean facts are fresh (`refs` are absent while stale).
3. **The "definitional choice" chip** on every card whose `uses` contains a definition (build.ts L680-682). It is **informational only, not clickable**.
4. **From the definition back to cards:** the item's "Used by" list (cards whose `uses` or `presupposes` include it, build.ts L780-791).
5. There are **no arrows** to definitions. The expanded card's "Depends on" / "Used by" list cards only, and "Rests on" lists only axioms (definitions never appear there).
6. Without Lean facts (syntactic mode, never checked) the definitions are still listed, but `uses` is absent. So there is no "uses:" line, no "definitional choice" chip, and every "Used by" is empty.

**Definitions that exist in Lean but are not shown as definitions:**
- **A card's own statement `abbrev n : Prop := S` and its `.holds`** are owned by the card and therefore excluded from the vocabulary. They appear only in that card's expanded "Lean" code box (`lean.code` = docstring mirror + statement + `.holds`; build.ts `codePieces` L190-205).
  - Another card's statement used inside this one appears as a reference arrow (on focus), as a clickable identifier that reveals that card, and as "mentioned in the statement" in Depends on.
  - Its vocabulary is folded into this card's `uses`.
- **Extra names on a multi-name `lean:` pin** are owned by the card (build.ts L319, L359). They are excluded from the vocabulary **and** not in the card's code (codePieces covers only the statement and `.holds`). So they have **no board representation at all**, and their bodies are not followed by the `uses` closure. (Only a user's hand edit can create these: the gate's markup rule stops Claude from writing such pins.)
- **A definition directly below a card's block** (adjacent binding, no blank line) is captured as that card's statement. It shows as "Lean problem" (TL113), not as a Definition.
- **Presupposition instances** are hidden. **Folded auxiliaries** show only inside their parent's code.
- **Other subjects' definitions** appear only if this subject's cards use them.
- **Presuppositions** (`T.exists`), which the Review's Definitions step asks about as "existence assumption", are under **Presuppositions** on the board, not under Definitions.
- **Proof-only definitions** are listed under Definitions without the "definition on a statement path" flag. They are never asked about in the Review.

**Relation to the Review's "Definitions" step:**
- The step (run/Review.tsx L120-169; DefinitionQuestion in core run.ts L377-393) asks about definitions that are new in the run **and** on a statement path, plus every new presupposition (gate/rules.ts `flagged` L808-834).
- Accept needs "Yes, I endorse it" for each. This is checked in the webview (`definitionsApproved`, model/run.ts L499-502) and again by the runner (manager.ts L1651-1652: "Answer every definition question: a “no” is feedback.").
- **The "yes" is never persisted.** After Accept the board keeps showing "definition on a statement path … needs your endorsement" and the "definitional choice" chip. Nothing in the code records an endorsement.

## 3. Card fields: shown where, editable how

| Field (TlNode / markup) | Shown | Editable on the board today | How |
|---|---|---|---|
| `naturalName` (`natural_name:`) | face | yes | F2 or expanded "Edit" → InlineEdit (aria "Edit the sentence"); one line, verbatim (`oneLine`); `editNode` field `naturalName`. The core planner also updates the statement docstring when it mirrored the old sentence, and pins `lean:` (planAction.ts L127-136). **Does not reset `worded_by: agent`** |
| `rationale` (`rationale:`) | face "because: …" | yes | "Add why"/"Edit why", or the "no reason yet"/"no source yet" chip → InlineEdit (placeholder "Leave empty to remove the reason"). Has no provenance marker |
| `stance` | expanded chips (Assumption, or any card with a stance set) | yes | toggle chips "I believe it" / "It's a rule or definition" / "Supposing, for argument"; clicking again clears |
| `source` (evidential) | expanded chips (non-Goal, or when set) | yes | "source:" "observed" / "reported" / "inferred" / "common knowledge" |
| `type` (kind) | column, glyph, stripe | yes, through dialogs | drag across columns; "Make Assumption/Derivation/Goal" (the two other kinds; tooltip = D-11 impact); "make Derivation?" chips. The dependents dialog and the "Why do you hold it?" rationale dialog may ask first. Changes Lean (`.holds` added or removed) |
| order (layout.json) | column order | yes | drag within the column; Alt+↑/↓ |
| `premises` (declared support) | dashed arrows; "Depends on (declared)" | **only through These suffice** | `startRun` replace or add; the host declares them (protocol.ts L152-157). No direct premise editor |
| delete | n/a | yes | Delete key or "Delete" → delete dialog |
| add | n/a | yes | A\|D\|G box (kind, sentence, optional stance/why/source; no LLM, no Lean) |
| `id` | **not shown** (only `data-node-id`; also in some diagnostic texts and the `@@ telelean` block) | no | slug of the first 6 words (core graph.ts L159-176), written as `id:` on add |
| Lean code / statement / `.holds` | expanded "Lean" box (Copy, Open in editor) | no (read-only; opens the editor) | |
| status (formal, proof, flags) | chips | no (derived) | |
| uses / refs / presupposes / axioms / externalUsers | uses line, code links, Presupposes, "Lean's axiom list", Used by | no (derived) | |
| Depends on / Used by / Rests on / Taken as hypotheses | expanded | no (derived) | buttons reveal cards |
| Attempts | expanded "Attempts (n)" | no | |
| `provenance.wordedBy` | italic + "(Claude's wording)" | no (a hand edit of the markup only) | |
| `body` (notes after `---`), `asserted`, `supersedes`, `refines`, `tags`, `origin`, `session`, `ext`, `certificates`, `provenance.endorsed` | **never shown** | no | |

Protocol-level whitelist: `EditableField = 'naturalName' | 'rationale' | 'stance' | 'source'` (core actions.ts L18; protocol.ts L280, L555). planEditNode refuses anything else: "This field cannot be edited on the board."

Vocabulary items have no markup block, so none of the card fields exist for them (no sentence, rationale, stance or source). Their fields are name/shortName, kind, type, arity, gloss (docstring; `glossBy` is always `'user'`, vocabulary.ts L333), code, usedBy, flags and loc. Nothing about a vocabulary item is editable on the board.

## 4. Selection, the tray, actions, and toolbar-like areas

### Selection model (state/store.ts)
- **What can be selected:** only cards (`selected: string[]` of node ids, in click order; L208-211).
  - Not selectable: vocabulary items, presupposition chips, ghosts, fields, review items.
  - Proposed-view cards are not selectable either: the proposed view is read-only (NodeCard L138-141; decisions-log L399).
  - Clicks inside the expanded area never change the selection (CardDetails `data-nodrag onClick={stop}` L335; decisions-log L136).
- **Gestures** (`clickCard` L1123-1131, NodeCard L139-181):
  - a plain click selects only that card (clicking the sole selected card again does nothing; there is no toggle-off);
  - Ctrl/Cmd+click toggles a card in or out;
  - Space on a focused card toggles it.
  - There is no Shift range select, no click-on-empty-board to clear, and no Escape to clear.
  - Clearing: the tray's "Clear" (`clearSelection`), a chip's × (`deselect`), a subject change (applyGraph L1081-1082), or a card vanishing from the graph.
- **Target:** an explicit target set with the ⊢ button on a premise chip (`setTarget`, no validation, L1147-1149). Otherwise the single selected GOAL (`trayModel` L457-471).
- Selection is **webview-only**:
  - not in the persisted webview state, which holds only subject, vocabCollapsed, requestCounter and runSplit (L76-86);
  - it is posted as `select`, which the host ignores (extension/src/logic/boardSession.ts L190-192).
- Selection also feeds arrow focus: `focusOf` = selected ∪ hovered (Board.tsx L54).

### Tray (tray/SelectionTray.tsx)
- **Empty hints:**
  - "No cards yet: type something you believe in the box below and press Enter. It becomes your first assumption."
  - otherwise: "Click a card to select it, Ctrl/Cmd-click to select several. Select premises and one goal, then press “These suffice”."
- **Full tray:**
  - "N selected";
  - premise chips, each with a ⊢ button (title "Make this the target") and × ("Remove from selection");
  - "⊢" and the target slot "target";
  - "+ presupposes:" chips;
  - buttons "Clear", "Add to its premises ▶" (only when "These suffice" would drop declared premises), then "Self-evident?" (a target and no premises) **or** "These suffice ▶";
  - "Starting the run…" or the blocked reason;
  - the warning "“These suffice” replaces the target’s declared premises and drops “…”." (L246-251).
- **While a run is active** the tray folds to one line: "n premises ⊢ “target”", a disabled button, the reason, and a chevron "Show the whole selection".

### What "These suffice" requires (trayModel L457-471, startRun L1384-1393)
- **A target.** Without one the reasons are:
  - "Several goals are selected: choose the target with ⊢."
  - "Choose the target (a Goal or a Derivation) with ⊢."
  - "Select the card to prove too: a Goal, or a Derivation (then choose it with ⊢)."
- **The target is not an ASSUMPTION** ("An assumption is something you hold: make it a Derivation first, then prove it.").
- **No active run in the model folder** (`trayRunBlock`, model/run.ts L45-59). For example, during review: "Claude's proposal is waiting for your review: accept, give feedback or discard it first."
- **Not already starting.**
- Premises are all the other selected cards, of any kind.
- On the host side: egress consent (a refusal starts "Not started:") and a preflight.

### Every action available today, and where it lives
- **Tray (acts on the selection):** Clear, × per chip, ⊢ make target, presupposition highlight, These suffice ▶ / Self-evident? / Add to its premises ▶, fold/unfold.
- **There is no multi-card delete, kind change, edit, freeze or suspend.**
- **Per card, on the face:** select, expand, drag (re-order or kind change), the chip buttons ("…make Derivation?", "no reason yet"), the ⚠ N badge, the "uses ▾" menu.
- **Per card, keyboard:** Enter expand, Space select, F2 edit, Delete delete dialog, Alt+↑/↓ re-order.
- **Per card, expanded:** Copy, Open in editor, identifier hover/click, problem "Open", relation buttons (reveal), "Show all n" attempts, stance and source chips, Make <Kind> ×2, Edit, Add why / Edit why, Delete.
- **Proposed view:** expand only, plus the text "This is Claude’s proposal (read-only): switch the board to “Current” to edit your cards." (CardDetails L358-360).

### Toolbar and menu areas
- **Header `.tl-toolbar`** (wraps): "telelean", root name, "subject: [S ▾]" (menu with "New subject…"), "History ▾", Undo/Redo icons, the Lean badge, "Problems N", the run badge, a spacer, then the Legend ("declared", "verified by Lean", "conditional", "mismatch", "formalised").
- **ProposalBanner**: "Claude’s proposal" with counts, "Current | Proposed" (radiogroup "Board shows"), "Review…", "Accept", "Feedback…", "Discard", "Raw Lean diff…".
- The **tray** and the **expanded-card action row** `.tl-details__actions`.
- **Dropdowns** via common/Popover.tsx (`.tl-menu`, role=menu, keyboard navigation, portal into body): subject, history, problems, uses.
- **No context menu exists**: no `onContextMenu`, no `webview/context` contribution. The only menu contribution is explorer/context "Initialize Model Here" (extension/package.json L47-54).

## 5. Visual conventions (styles/board.css)

**Variables** (L11-36), all VS Code theme variables with fallbacks:
- `--tl-kind-a/d/g` ← `telelean.kindAssumption/Derivation/Goal` (purple, green, orange);
- `--tl-aura` ← `telelean.formalizedAura` (blue #3794FF dark);
- `--tl-vocab` ← `telelean.vocabulary` (teal);
- `--tl-highlight` ← `telelean.highlight` (orange-ish);
- `--tl-warn`, `--tl-error`, `--tl-info`;
- `--tl-diff-added/changed/removed` (git colours);
- `--tl-edge`, `--tl-edge-focus` (focusBorder).

The contributed colours are in extension/package.json L187-216 (one-dot ids). test/unit/theme.test.ts whitelists exactly the M0 + M1 ids, so a new colour needs that test updated.

**Card states and the CSS property each one uses:**
- **Formalised aura** `.tl-card[data-formal='formalized']`: `box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--tl-aura), 0 0 10px 2px …` (L349-351). The legend swatch `.tl-legend__aura` is at L132-138.
- **Selected** `[data-selected]`: tinted background + `outline: 2px solid var(--vscode-focusBorder)` (L343-347) + the check glyph (L375-382, comment: "the aura is blue too").
- **Highlight flash** `[data-highlight]`: outline in `--tl-highlight` + background-image tint + a 2 s animation (L465-479).
- **Diff** `[data-diff]`: box-shadow ring and halo in `--tl-diff`. When combined with the aura: `0 0 0 1px aura, 0 0 0 3px diff, glow` (L1472-1476). "removed" adds line-through.
- **Provisional** `[data-provisional]`: dashed border (L462).
- **Dragging**: opacity .45. **Drop edge**: `::after` line.
- **Kind**: `::before` stripe.
- **Ghost** `.tl-ghost`: opacity .86, background 70%, kind-A border and stripe at 50% (L1483-1506; "never dashed").
- **Proposed view**: list tint (L1454).
- **Vocabulary item**: 3px teal left border, warn colour when `[data-warn]` (L657-665).
- **Chips**: tones lean (aura colour), attention (warning), error, info (dashed border), subtle (italic).
- **Arrows**: declared `stroke-dasharray: 5 4` (L731), reference thin, focus focusBorder 2.25 (L734-736), conditional hollow head (L745).
- **Claude's words**: italic + marker (`.tl-agent__marker`, `.tl-card__agent-marker`, `data-provenance="agent"`).

**High contrast** (L1559-1600):
- aura → `outline 2px`; selection → inset box-shadow; highlight → dashed outline; diff → outline; ghost → opaque.
- Reduced motion turns the flash animation off.

**Channels already in use:** outer box-shadow (aura, diff), outline (selection, focus, highlight, HC aura and diff), border style (provisional), `::before` (kind), `::after` (drop edge), background-image (flash), opacity (ghost, dragging), italics (Claude). The free channels for a FROZEN mark are an inner (inset) ring outside HC, a row icon like the selection check, or a new word or chip.

The run panel already uses `codicon-lock` for the statement-freeze activity (RunPanel.tsx L243), and "freeze" or "frozen" already means the run's statement freeze (`freeze_statements`, "Statements frozen (round N)", the G4 check "statement unchanged").

## 6. Facts that matter for implementing the spec
- **Board edits go straight to files**, through host messages: `addNode`, `editNode`, `kindChange`, `reorder`, `deleteNode`, `undo`, `redo`, `startRun`. They are optimistic and rolled back on refusal (store.ts L1-11). The host treats webview input as untrusted (protocol.ts L35).
- The user **can edit the Current board while a run is active**; Accept rebases (D-16, D-21). Adding from the box switches the board back to Current (store.ts L1290).
- On a new proposal the board switches to Proposed unless a drag or edit is in progress (applyProposal L961). Switching to Proposed ends edits and drags (L1453-1459).
- **Accept is all-or-nothing.** Only lifecycle items can be ticked, and every definition question needs a "yes".

## 7. Docs vs code (the code is authoritative)
- **Card face.** 03 §7 lists a "checkbox (select)", "certificate badges", "⚑ decision chips", "wording history" and "Shiki". The code has click-select with a check glyph, no certificate badges, no decision chips, no wording history, and a plain `<pre>`.
- **Toolbar.** 03 §7's "search/filter · edges Auto|Focus|All · ancestors/consequences" and the "Ask Claude…" composer are absent.
- **Context menu.** D-17 "Move to ▸ … in the context menu" and 03 §7 "context-menu equivalents, contributed as VS Code keybindings" are not implemented. The keys are handled inside the webview.
- **Arrows.** D-13 "drag from a port" and the junction dot are absent (user-guide §8: "No drawing arrows by dragging").
- **ARIA.** 03 §7 says grid/treegrid; the code uses list/listitem.
- **Colour id.** 03 §7 names `telelean.node.formalizedAura`; the code has `telelean.formalizedAura`.
- **Review placement.** 03 §7 puts the review "in place on the cards"; the code puts it in the run panel, with a read-only overlay on the board.
- **Agent glosses.** D-3 and project-report L669 say Claude's glosses of new vocabulary are styled as Claude's. In core, `glossBy` is always `'user'` (vocabulary.ts L333), so on the board (group, tooltips, uses menu, the statement step's "It uses") they render in user styling. Only the Review's "New vocabulary" and "Definitions" steps force AgentText. The AT6.10 test passes because its fixtures hand-set `glossBy: 'agent'` (test/shared/runs.ts L210, L285, L389).
- **Editing an adopted card.** User guide 10.9 and m2-plan L374 say the "Claude's wording" mark goes away after you edit the sentence. In code `worded_by: agent` stays (planEditNode never touches it; confirmed in project-report L2409).

answers:
Question 3: where do "definitions" show up in the main card graph?

They appear only inside the Vocabulary group, in its "Definitions" section. That group is at the top of the Assumptions (left) column, after any "Claude suggests" ghost cards and before the cards (packages/webview/src/board/Column.tsx L95-100). It is a list of boxes, not cards, and is collapsed by default (store.ts L1005-1006). There is no Definitions column, no definition card, and no arrow between a definition and a card.

What counts as a definition (core/src/project/vocabulary.ts L262-275):
- def, abbrev, structure, inductive/coinductive, class and instance declarations that are not bound to any card.
- This includes a Prop-valued def/abbrev with no @@ block (an "untracked statement"). Its .holds axiom then shows under "Unmarked axioms" as a "hidden assumption".

The section is shown only when:
- the vocabulary is not empty (VocabularyGroup.tsx L183), and
- at least one definition exists, and
- the group is open: you click the "Vocabulary" toggle, a highlight opens it, or, in the Proposed view, the proposal adds vocabulary.

What each definition box shows:
- its short name and type, and its docstring as the gloss;
- flags, notably "definition on a statement path" (tooltip: "A definition your statements rely on (D-4: needs your endorsement)");
- when expanded: its source code, "Used by" (the cards whose statements rely on it) and "Open in editor".

How you get from a card to its definitions:
- **The card's "uses:" line.** It lists the statement's vocabulary, definitions included, following definitions transitively. "▾ N" lists every item with its kind ("definition") and gloss. Picking one opens the group, scrolls to the item and flashes it.
- **Identifiers in the expanded Lean code.** Hover shows the gloss and "definition · name : type"; a click highlights the item.
- **The "definitional choice" chip** on any card whose statement uses a definition. It is information only and cannot be clicked.

These links need Lean facts. In syntactic mode, or before the first check, the definitions are listed but no card links to them.

What is not shown as a definition:
- A card's own `abbrev n : Prop := S` and its `.holds` belong to the card. They appear only in that card's expanded "Lean" box, never in the Vocabulary group.
- Extra names on a multi-name `lean:` pin have no board representation at all.
- A def placed directly below a card's block becomes that card's statement and shows as "Lean problem".
- Presupposition instances and structure fields or constructors are not listed separately.
- Existence assumptions (`T.exists`), which the Review's "Definitions" step lists as "existence assumption", are under "Presuppositions" on the board.

After Accept:
- Your "Yes, I endorse it" from the Review is not stored anywhere.
- The board keeps showing "definition on a statement path … needs your endorsement" and the "definitional choice" chip.

The word "definition" means different things on the board:
- the stance chip "It's a rule or definition" is a card's stance, unrelated to Lean definitions;
- the "Definitions" section is Lean declarations;
- the "definitional choice" chip is on cards;
- the Review's "Definitions" step lives in the run panel, not the board.

Question 1: what the "Fully explicit" checkbox does

It is on each Statement step of the Review, in the run panel (Review.tsx L55-58). Its tooltip is "No notation, every argument and universe shown, no coercion arrows".

- It is a display toggle for that one statement (store `review.explicit[nodeId]`).
- It switches the shown Lean from Lean's normal `#print` to the same `#print` with these options: `set_option pp.explicit true`, `pp.notation false`, `pp.universes true`, `pp.coercions false`. They are produced by the runner in a scratch check (runner/src/gate/scratch.ts L112, L123-141).
- The effect: implicit arguments are shown, `¬ p` reads `Not (p)`, universe levels are shown, and ↑ arrows are hidden in favour of explicit coercion functions.
- If Lean could not print the statement, both forms fall back to the source text, so they can look identical (runner proposal/service.ts L232-233).
- It changes no file, no proof and nothing about Accept. It exists so you can check the meaning without notation hiding anything.

Question 2: "Claude suggests" vs "Statement 1, Statement 2"

"Statement N" steps (Review.tsx; runner service.ts L211-239):
- There is one step per card whose Lean statement is new or changed in this round. It is labelled just "Statement" when there is only one.
- Each asks "Does the Lean say what the sentence says?": your sentence beside Claude's Lean, with "Fully explicit", the "It uses" list and "Show on the board".
- It is a meaning check of Claude's formalisation of cards: the target, the selected premises, and adopted suggestions.
- There is no accept or decline per statement. Accept takes the whole proposal.

"Claude suggests" cards are ghosts (core run.ts L235-254):
- They are new premises Claude proposes, which you have not stated. Each comes with a Lean check that your selected premises plus it prove the target ("closes the gap (checked)"). A flag "gives the goal on its own" warns when it may just restate the goal.
- They are not part of the proposal's files: no card id, no arrows. They appear translucent at the top of the Assumptions column in the Proposed view, and in the report card.
- You decide each one: "I hold this" (with an optional reason) or "No".
- Adopting starts a new round. The suggestion is written as an Assumption marked as Claude's wording and added to the target's premises, and Claude proves the target again.
- In the next proposal it is a normal new card and gets its own "Statement" step.

In short: statements check Claude's translation of your cards; ghosts ask whether you want to adopt a new belief. The LLM never adds beliefs on its own (D-6).
